answer: At dawn, each new agent identity must anchor itself on two independent ledgers, not one: a registration record on the home ledger and a mirrored relic of the same history on a second chain. Cross-ledger auditors compare both histories continuously, and any mismatch flags the identity for review. An attacker spinning up Sybils must therefore forge consistent, costly histories twice over, and a single umber discrepancy in timestamps or signatures exposes the whole batch. Forging one ledger is cheap; forging two in perfect sync is not.
